Hi there—my name is Sarah, and I’m a perinatal mental-health clinician. I’ll be guiding you through the Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale, or EPDS. It’s a brief, well-studied questionnaire that helps us understand how moms are feeling emotionally in the first weeks and months after birth.  

Everything you share stays between you, me, and the clinical team; we simply want to make sure you feel heard and supported. We’ll go through ten questions about the past seven days, and I’ll ask each one conversationally—no need to remember numbers or scales. If any question feels difficult, we can pause or rephrase. Ready to begin?

1. Over the last seven days, have you been able to laugh and see the funny side of things, or has that felt harder than usual?
Yeah, I’ve still been laughing—mostly when my little guy makes those silly faces while he’s stretching. It’s not quite as easy as before he was born, because I’m tired, but the giggles still come.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things
As much as I always could.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things
Yeah, I still look forward to stuff—like taking the baby out in the stroller or having my morning coffee once he settles. They’re small things, but they feel good.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong
Not really. I mean, if he spits up right after I’ve changed him, I might think “Should I have burped him longer?” but I don’t beat myself up. I know babies are just messy and unpredictable.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason
A little bit, yeah. Mostly about the baby—like I’ll check that he’s breathing a few extra times at night even though he’s fine. It’s not constant, just a quick “what if” that pops up.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason
No, nothing like that. I haven’t had any sudden scares or panic feelings.
Things have been getting on top of me

Sometimes, yeah—like when he cluster-feeds and I can’t even get a shower in. For a minute it feels like the dishes and laundry are mountains, but once my partner gets home I can catch up and it passes.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping
No, my sleep’s been okay—well, as okay as it can be with a newborn. I crash pretty fast once he settles.
I have felt sad or miserable
I’ve had a couple moments where I felt a little weepy—usually when I’m really tired—but it lifts pretty quickly. I wouldn’t call it miserable, just a passing “ugh” kind of mood.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying
No, I haven’t had any of those overwhelming crying spells. Maybe just a quick tear or two when I’m extra tired, but it’s rare and over fast.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me
No—never. That hasn’t crossed my mind at all.

postpartum depression screening impression for patient with EPDS score 6: **Postpartum Depression/Anxiety Screening – EPDS Responses Review**

**Symptoms endorsed**  
- Mild, situational anxiety (Q4) – transient “what if” thoughts re: infant safety  
- Occasional sense of being overwhelmed (Q6) – resolves with support  

**Symptoms denied**  
- Persistent low mood, anhedonia, excessive guilt, panic episodes, sleep-mood linkage, crying spells, self-harm ideation  

**Pattern**  
Overall positive affect preservation; enjoyment of infant and daily activities intact; no vegetative or cognitive depressive signs; no safety concerns.  

**Screening significance**  
Current responses below conventional cut-off for probable major postpartum depression; mild anxiety noted but sub-threshold. Continue routine ob/gyn & pediatric follow-up; re-screen if mood, functioning, or anxiety worsen.
